correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs the full reduced-Laplacian cokernel by exact generator-and-relation elimination, including the sink-row redundancy, \(t=1\), \(q=1\) boundaries and \(\gcd(C,n)=1\). The integer Smith checker re-derived the factors for 44 \( (n,t) \) pairs through \(n=10\); separate exact Smith computations additionally covered 65 pairs through \(n=12\). Computations are finite corroboration, not the universal argument.

evidence: Jacobson–Niedermaier–Reiner (J. Graph Theory 44 (2003), 231–250) applies to complete multipartite graphs including K_{n,n}; deleting any cross-edge makes G_{n,t} non-complete multipartite.
Dong–Jiang–Guo (arXiv:2409.02654, Definition 2.3) explicitly specify complete bipartite joins between consecutive parts of a multipartite chain, not isolated missing cross-edges.
General Smith algorithms for an arbitrary integer matrix can in principle evaluate any example, but are not an explicit n,t invariant-factor determination.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither cited structural family contains G_{n,t} for 1≤t<n. An algorithm to compute SNF from any supplied matrix is not itself an explicit formula for the full parameter family.

originality.rationale: Specific published full matching-deletion and complete-bipartite endpoint theorems were read and compared by implication. Their \(t=0\) or \(t=n\) statements do not determine the invariant factors of the nonregular intermediate graph family. Another article on multipartite chain graphs has different adjacencies. Searches of published mathematical results and mathematical record matches found no covering classification; unindexed equivalent work remains a risk.
residual_risks: An older differently named family (nearly complete bicliques, partial crown graphs) could have an equivalent unpublished or poorly indexed formula.
The 2003 complete-multipartite paper was checked by metadata and known hypotheses rather than independently obtaining and reading its entire original full text.

value.rationale: A complete natural graph invariant for all intermediate edge deletions, with explicit finite abelian invariant factors and a multiplicative tree-count consequence, bridges known regular endpoints. The torsion-transition pattern distinguishes different deletion counts; neither finite checking nor routine determinant computation gives these integral group structures.
